from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Coherent light maintains a stable phase relationship.",
            "Superposition creates fixed interference nodes and anti-nodes.",
            "Path difference between waves determines constructive interference."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light", lecture_lines)

        # Animations
        # Create wave sources
        source1 = Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(self.grid["C2"])
        source2 = Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(self.grid["D2"])
        
        # Create waves (circles)
        waves1 = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=r, color="#FF00FF", stroke_opacity=0.5) for r in [0.5, 1.0, 1.5]])
        waves1.move_to(source1)
        waves2 = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=r, color="#FF00FF", stroke_opacity=0.5) for r in [0.5, 1.0, 1.5]])
        waves2.move_to(source2)

        # Highlight regions
        constructive = Dot(self.grid["C4"], color="#FFFF00")
        destructive = Dot(self.grid["D4"], color="#00FF00")
        
        label_c = Text("Constructive", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(constructive, UP)
        label_d = Text("Destructive", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(destructive, UP)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), FadeIn(source1), FadeIn(source2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"),
            Create(waves1),
            Create(waves2)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            FadeIn(constructive),
            FadeIn(label_c)
        )
        self.play(
            FadeIn(destructive),
            FadeIn(label_d),
            constructive.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            destructive.animate.set_color("#00FF00")
        )

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Diffraction: The Bending of Light", [
            "Diffraction is the bending of waves around obstacles.",
            "Huygens-Fresnel principle: each point acts as a source.",
            "Slits cause light to spread into an intensity pattern."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "#00FFFF: Display a thin vertical slit on the screen."
        # "#FF00FF: Draw a series of incoming parallel plane waves toward the slit."
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        slit = Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(slit, 'C2')
        self.play(Create(slit))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        waves = VGroup(*[Line(LEFT*0.5, RIGHT*0.5, color="#FF00FF").shift(LEFT*2 + i*0.3) for i in range(5)])
        self.add(waves)
        self.play(waves.animate.shift(RIGHT*1.5), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "#FFFF00: Animate waves emerging from the slit, spreading in a semi-circular pattern."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Simplified representation
        circles = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=0.2 + i*0.2, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=PI, color="#FFFF00") for i in range(3)])
        circles.move_to(slit.get_center())
        self.play(Create(circles), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "#00FF00: Display an intensity pattern curve '#00FF00' appearing on a distant vertical wall."
        # "#FFFFFF: Fade in the label 'Diffraction Pattern' above the curve."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        wall = Line(UP*1.5, DOWN*1.5, color=WHITE).shift(RIGHT*3)
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sinc(x*2), x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color="#00FF00")
        curve.rotate(PI/2).shift(RIGHT*2.5)
        
        self.play(Create(wall), Create(curve))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        label = Text("Diffraction Pattern", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label.next_to(curve, UP)
        self.play(FadeIn(label))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", [
            "Holograms are diffraction patterns stored on media.", 
            "They enable secure data storage and advanced imaging.", 
            "Holographic displays project information onto real-world views."
        ])
        
        # Mobjects
        hologram_placeholder = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        security_sticker = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=PURPLE).set_fill(PURPLE, opacity=0.5)
        hud_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
        app_text = Text("Holographic Applications: Security, Storage", font_size=24, color=GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(hologram_placeholder, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(hologram_placeholder), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(security_sticker, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        ray = Line(start=self.grid['D2'], end=self.grid['D6'], color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(security_sticker), Create(ray), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(hud_arrow, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(GrowArrow(hud_arrow), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # Final flashes and fade
        self.play(Write(app_text.move_to(self.grid['B4'])), self.lecture.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(hologram_placeholder), FadeOut(security_sticker), FadeOut(ray), FadeOut(hud_arrow), FadeOut(app_text))

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly revisit superposition and path difference. Explain that coherent light (lasers) maintains a constant phase relationship, which is the foundational requirement for interference.
sections.example: Visualizing two ripples in a pond intersecting to create fixed nodes and anti-nodes.

sections.title: Diffraction: The Bending of Light
sections.content: Define diffraction as the spreading of waves around obstacles. Use Huygens-Fresnel principle to explain how every point on a wavefront acts as a secondary source.
sections.example: Animation showing a laser beam passing through a tiny slit, spreading into a characteristic 'sinc function' intensity pattern on a wall.

sections.title: Holography: Recording the Interference Pattern
sections.content: Explain that while standard photography captures only amplitude (brightness), holography records both amplitude and phase by interfering an object beam with a reference beam.
sections.example: A 3D model of a 'Cyber-Owl' robot: showing the reference beam (direct light) and object beam (reflected light) meeting at the film plate to form complex interference fringes.

sections.title: Reconstruction: The Diffraction Gate
sections.content: Describe the hologram as a 'complex diffraction grating.' When illuminated by the reference beam, the interference fringes diffract light to recreate the original wavefronts, tricking the eye into seeing a 3D image.
sections.example: An animation of a light beam hitting a 'holographic credit card sticker,' where the fringes act as a gate that bends light into the exact shape of the original 3D object.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Summarize that a hologram is essentially a diffraction pattern stored on a medium. Discuss real-world uses in data storage and security.
sections.example: Visualizing a futuristic HUD (Heads-Up Display) in a character's helmet that uses holographic diffraction to project navigation arrows onto the real-world view.
